criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Nine genuinely distinct constructions and a register (torn paper, punch card, sockets) that shares nothing with the last fortnight's limestone, high bay and caliche decks. Against that: slide 4's dek overflows its brown plate onto cream at ~1.1:1 contrast; slide 6's `will` boxes butt the next word so the deck's key frame reads `willsupport` and `willbe`; slide 2 paints the deck's strongest blue on the shortfall and washes the achievement; slides 8 and 9 have large dead zones (slide 8 is empty cream from roughly y=940 to y=1350).

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces: 66 to c2, 34.82/51.16 to c3, 95/760/110,960 to c5 and c6, 45 million to c8, 12 and 8 to c9. The rejected list is unusually disciplined, refusing the county, the 'fastest university supercomputer' framing and the power figure. But slide 4's qualifier renders invisible, so c8 (confidence medium) reaches the reader stripped of its hedge, and the caption converts c16's 'is expected to begin' into flat present tense.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: The learnable sentence lands. The action does not: c14 ('actively seeking beta testing participants') is cited on slide 9 and never appears in slide 9's copy, so the one thing a reader could do today is withheld. c7 quotes the West Campus Data Center and no slide names it, so the deck names the body and no place at all. The public-money stake sits split across slides 4 and 8 and is never assembled in one sentence.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The arc is legible and the turn genuinely lands at 6, not 7. Slide 5 is the frame I would cut: empty dek in copy.json, one fact printed twice from two sources, sitting immediately before the turn. The cover earns its swipe on a riddle rather than on a subject, and 8 and 9 are two similarly sparse text-block frames so the deck coasts into its close.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and forensic with no boosterism and no doom. 'Read the verb.' and 'Not one of them is punched.' are real lines. No first person, no dashes, straight quotes, and the colon and semicolon on slide 7 are verbatim in c12 and c20. But nothing here sounds written from Texas rather than from a documents desk, and not one technical term is glossed (PFlop/s, Rmax, Rpeak, DGX, H200) in the state TEXAS_ATTITUDES section 9 says never to assume literacy in.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The palette and register are a real departure from the recent window. Structurally it is still the house move: topics.json's own 08-29 angle_note warns 'the next run should spend an opening move that is not an absence', which the cover honours, but both closing frames land on 'is not published' and 'No date is published for it', and the document-language forensic is flagged in the ledger across 08-19, 08-22 and 08-26.

hard_fails: Unfinished frame, slide 4: the second sentence of the S4 dek in copy.json, 'No meeting date is published for that approval.', overflows the brown plate onto the cream page and renders at roughly 1.1:1 contrast with the torn deckle edge cutting its glyphs. It is illegible in out/2026-09-03/render/slide-04.png. The frame therefore presents c8 (confidence: medium, and explicitly not a dated governing-body vote per claims.json's rejected list) with its only qualifier invisible.
one_sentence_fix: Put c14's 'actively seeking beta testing participants' on slide 9 in place of one line of the WHAT HAPPENS NEXT block, because the claim is already fetched and already cited on that frame and it turns the deck's honest non-answer into the one thing a Texan researcher can actually do today.
